India's Education Minister, Dharmendra Pradhan, has resigned after a week of mass demonstrations, handing a major victory to a new youth movement that has posed an unprecedented challenge to Narendra Modi's government.

In a statement released on Saturday afternoon, Pradhan said he had submitted his resignation letter to the Prime Minister in response to mounting pressure from students.

"Considering the situation that has arisen at Jantar Mantar and across the country, so that anti-national forces do not take advantage of this situation (...) I have submitted my resignation letter to the Prime Minister," Pradhan wrote in a social media post.

He said he had been "deeply saddened by what has unfolded over the past 10 days," adding: "I deeply respect the aspirations, feelings, and legitimate expectations of the country's youth."

During his 12 years in power, Modi has cultivated a strongman image and consistently maintained that his ministers are not accountable to public pressure. This marks the first time that a mass protest movement has forced one of his closest allies to resign.

The protests were organized by the newly formed youth political movement, the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), which has grown into a nationwide youth uprising this week.

The movement's central demand was Pradhan's resignation over an exam leak scandal that has affected millions of students and reportedly contributed to more than a dozen student suicides.

Modi's refusal to dismiss his minister over the scandal was widely viewed as a symbol of the alleged lack of accountability within the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and its repeated failure to address the challenges facing young people, particularly within India's troubled education system.

CJP organizers confirmed they had called off their demonstration following Pradhan's resignation and a meeting with senior BJP ministers on Saturday afternoon.

Addressing crowds gathered at the Jantar Mantar protest site in Delhi, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke praised the "courage" of students who turned out in huge numbers despite facing police violence.

🔊 Iran condemns US attacks on rescue vessels as breach of humanitarian law

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iran’s High Council for Human Rights has condemned deliberate US attacks on two Iranian maritime search-and-rescue vessels, saying the strikes constituted a grave violation of international humanitarian law and the rules governing humanitarian relief operations.

In a statement on Sunday, the top human rights body said the two vessels were targeted by US forces in the early hours of Thursday while conducting humanitarian search-and-rescue missions in Iran’s territorial waters.
​
According to the statement, the vessels were exclusively assigned to locating and rescuing people in distress at sea and had no connection to military operations.
​
The council said intentionally targeting such vessels amounted to a serious breach of fundamental principles of international humanitarian law, as well as the legal protections afforded to humanitarian rescue operations.
​
It cited Article 27 of the 1949 Second Geneva Convention, which provides protection for small boats and vessels used by governments or officially recognized coastal rescue institutions, arguing that such craft must be respected and protected.
​
The statement said safeguarding humanitarian and rescue operations was a fundamental obligation under international humanitarian law and warned that attacks on search-and-rescue capabilities could endanger the lives of civilians and emergency personnel.
